To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new technique to simultaneously diffuse Zn and Cd into InGaAs, which results in the generation of a shallow- and high doped p-type region.
the Zn acceptor diffusion is enhanced by the presence of a Cd acceptor, whereas the diffusion depth of the Cd acceptor is reduced by the presence of Zn acceptor.
we have demonstrated the possibility of the simultaneous diffusion of two different impurities in InGaAs by using a Zn3As/Cd3As source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diffusion of Zn and of Cd in InGa(As)P.
the diffusion of Zn and the simultaneous diffusion of Cd and Zn from a Cd3As2/Zn3As2 source into lattice-matched VPE InGa0.53Ga0.47As. A
the simultaneous diffusion of zinc and cadmium in III-V compounds, especially in InGaAs and InP, which is of interest in device technology, especially in high-speed and optoelectronic applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Zn atoms diffuse interstitially in the InGaAs lattice and that the Zn atoms are trapped at As antisite defects.

the diffusion of Zn and/or Cd in InGaP, InGaAs and InGaAsP is a very complex process, which can only be understood by taking into account the diffusion of the interstitials and the substitutionals as well as their mutual interaction.
the diffusion mechanism of the Zn and Cd atoms is interstitial-substitution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Zn diffusion in InGaAs is very similar to the Zn diffusion in GaAs.
we could realise the first simultaneous diffusion of Zn (acceptor) and Cd (donor) in InGaAs.
a new diffusion method for shallow- and high-p-doped regions in InGaAs is presented, which is based on a Zn/Cd diffusion couple.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cd interstitials are the dominant species for Cd diffusion in InGaAs, and the diffusion coefficient of the Cd interstitial is about 2 orders of magnitude smaller than that of the Zn acceptor.
the diffusion method is a suitable tool for the generation of a shallow- and high doped p-type region during controllable diffusion time.
the Cd atoms whose interstitution diffusion coefficient is smaller compared with that of Zn interstitials, can penetrate into the crystal up to the same depth as Zn atoms.
